summary:
We built an interactive, SI-powered web dashboard that turns decades of NASA microgravity combustion research into clear, fast fire-safety insights for human space exploration. In space, fire behaves very differently: flames become round, can spread at lower oxygen levels and can even keep burning invisibly as "cool flames." NASA has studied this in many experiments, but the results are scattered and hard to compare.

Our dashboard summarizes key NASA investigations (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, FLEX and SAME) as simple experiment cards showing the fuel, oxygen level, airflow and main findings. A comparison table shows how experiments are similar or different, and our Moon-Base Fire Risk Meter ranks findings by how important they are for future lunar habitats. An AI assistant answers questions in seconds, using only our NASA-based knowledge file, always shows its NASA source, and works offline in Google Chrome.

This matters because Moon bases will likely use air with 30% or more oxygen, making materials more flammable. Our tool helps scientists, students and engineers find NASA's fire lessons quickly, keeping astronauts safer on the Moon, Mars and beyond.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

Flame in Freefall is a website that summarizes, ranks and interprets NASA's research on fire in microgravity, to help keep crews safe on the Moon and Mars.

- Experiment Cards: 7 cards (BASS, BASS-II, Saffire, FLEX, SAME, ACME and the 1997 Mir fire) showing the fuel, oxygen, airflow, key finding, why it matters for the Moon and Mars, and the NASA source.

- Comparison Table: all experiments side by side, sortable, with our Moon-base relevance rating (1–5).

- Moon-Base Fire Risk Meter: users change oxygen, airflow, gravity and material and see the fire risk change, with the NASA finding behind each change.

- FlameBot: an AI chat assistant that answers questions in seconds using only our NASA knowledge file, and shows the source. It works offline.

KEY NASA FINDINGS

- BASS: turning off airflow put flames out quickly.

- BASS-II: flames survived at 17% oxygen in space vs 18% on Earth.

- Saffire: the largest fires ever lit in space showed that size changes results.

- FLEX: discovered invisible "cool flames."

- SAME: many smoke particles are tiny, and some detectors missed them.

- ACME: tested oxygen up to 85%.

IMPACT

Helps researchers, students and engineers find NASA fire results in seconds, supports safer Moon bases and rovers, and helps on Earth with better smoke detectors and firefighting.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS and JavaScript; Chrome's built-in AI (Gemini Nano) with a keyword-search backup; Visual Studio Code with Claude; NASA PSI and NTRS data.

CREATIVITY

It follows the challenge's three verbs (Summarize, Rank, Interpret) and lets users interact with the science through the Risk Meter and FlameBot.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED

Accuracy (NASA sources only), honesty (FlameBot says "I don't know" instead of guessing), Moon conditions (30%+ oxygen), and scope (no rocket engine fires).
